claim_scope: Transcribed server-held configuration for the two launch providers D-055 fixes. Nothing in this repository has performed an authorization request against either provider, so every capability below is recorded unverified and no control in ADR-015 that is conditional on a capability may be relied on yet. This file proves that the configuration an OAuth transaction binds is declared in one place and agrees with the SQL, OpenAPI and reason-code owners; it proves nothing about either provider's live behaviour.

rfc9207_iss.basis: No authorization response from GitHub has been observed in this repository, and docs/research/ records no primary-source reading of RFC 9207 support. ADR-015 makes a missing iss a failure only for a provider recorded as supporting it, so recording `supported` here without an observation would manufacture the control it is supposed to prove.

device_flow.basis: The GitHub App device path is named as an open question in ADR-015's reopening conditions and in the open-research list of docs/security/AUTHENTICATION_AND_RECOVERY.md. Nothing has been polled.

rfc9207_iss.basis: No authorization response from X has been observed in this repository. This row and GitHub's are deliberately identical on this field: the two callback operations previously differed in whether they declared `iss` at all, and no record anywhere said why, so the asymmetry was a capability claim nothing backed.

device_flow.basis: X/Twitter sign-in protocol and long-term API constraints are an open research item in docs/security/AUTHENTICATION_AND_RECOVERY.md. Nothing has been polled.
